title: Static import modules shared with the service worker chunk — dynamic import injects a document polyfill that crashes the SW
trigger: An MV3 extension module is imported by both a DOM context (popup/content-script) and the service worker, and a caller uses dynamic import()
principle: In an MV3 extension with multiple entry points (SW, content-script, popup, sidepanel, offscreen), a module can live in a shared chunk imported by both DOM and non-DOM contexts. Vite injects modulepreload-polyfill (which uses document) into any chunk containing a dynamic import(). If that chunk is reachable from the SW, the SW loads the polyfill, hits ReferenceError: document is not defined, and registration fails (status 15) — killing all content-script messaging. Rule: for any module shared with the SW bundle, always static import. Dynamic import is only safe for modules NOT reachable from the SW (UI-only modules used solely by popup/sidepanel).

cases.context: A controller adds a dynamic import for a settings store that is already statically imported elsewhere and also imported by the SW via helpers → Vite injects modulepreload-polyfill into the shared settingsStore chunk → SW crashes on document reference

applyFor: MV3 extensions bundled with Vite / @crxjs/vite-plugin (or any bundler that auto-injects polyfill based on dynamic import)
Modules shared between the SW and content-script/popup (settings store, message bus, chrome API wrappers)
Code-splitting decisions — when dynamic import is safe (UI-only) vs when static import is mandatory (SW-reachable)
Diagnosing "Service worker registration failed. Status code: 15" + "Receiving end does not exist" after adding a dynamic import
